explanations: Correct. BD/DC = AB/AC = 6/8 = 3/4, so BD = 3 and DC = 4; then AD^2 = 6*8-3*4 = 36, giving AD = 6.
Incorrect. 4*sqrt(3) is sqrt(48), i.e. sqrt(AB*AC) - it omits the BD*DC correction entirely.
Incorrect. 5 assumes the bisector also bisects the side (BD = DC = 3.5), which holds only for isosceles triangles.
Incorrect. 7 is BC itself - reported instead of the cevian.
items.prompt: In triangle ABC, AB = 6, AC = 8 and BC = 7. The internal bisector of angle A meets BC at D. Find the length AD.
items.solution: 1. By the angle-bisector theorem, BD/DC = AB/AC = 6/8 = 3/4, so BD = 3 and DC = 4. 2. Bisector length: AD^2 = AB*AC-BD*DC = 48-12 = 36. 3. AD = 6 (check by Stewart: 36*4+64*3 = 7*(AD^2+12) gives AD^2 = 36). Answer A.

explanations: Incorrect. 225/17 is PM, the distance from P to the chord - the wrong segment.
Incorrect. 120/17 is the half-chord - reported without doubling.
Incorrect. 64/17 is OM, the distance from the centre to the chord.
items.prompt: From an external point P, tangents are drawn to a circle of radius 8 cm. The distance from P to the centre O is 17 cm. If the points of contact are A and B, find the length of the chord AB.
items.solution: 1. Tangent length = sqrt(OP^2-r^2) = sqrt(289-64) = 15. 2. If M is where OP meets AB: AM = r*tangent/OP = 8*15/17 = 120/17. 3. Chord AB = 2*AM = 240/17. Answer B.

explanations: Incorrect. 3 counts only the positive factor pairs (1,12), (2,6), (3,4), forgetting each negates too.
Correct. Factor pairs of 12 with both signs: (1,12),(2,6),(3,4),(-1,-12),(-2,-6),(-3,-4); p is minus their sum: -13,-8,-7,13,8,7 - six values.
Incorrect. 4 has no basis here; every factor pair (and its negation) yields a distinct p.
Incorrect. 12 double-counts: (a,b) and (b,a) give the same sum, hence the same p.
items.prompt: The equation x^2 + px + 12 = 0 has integer roots. How many distinct possible values can p take?
items.solution: 1. Integer roots r, s with rs = 12 and p = -(r+s). 2. Factor pairs of 12: (1,12),(2,6),(3,4) and their negations. 3. Sums: 13, 8, 7, -13, -8, -7 - all distinct, so six values of p. Answer B.

items.prompt: Find the sum of all real values of k for which the equation |x^2 - 4| = k has exactly three real solutions in x.
items.solution: 1. y = |x^2-4| is W-shaped: zeros at x = +-2, local max 4 at x = 0. 2. y = k meets it: 0 solutions for k < 0; 2 for k = 0; 4 for 0 < k < 4; 2 for k > 4. 3. Exactly 3 only at k = 4 (x = 0, +-2*sqrt(2)). 4. Sum = 4. Answer: 4

explanations: Incorrect. 36 seconds uses the speed DIFFERENCE (30 km/h), i.e. same-direction motion - wrong for approaching trains.
Incorrect. 12 seconds divides 300 by 25, treating km/h figures as m/s without conversion.
Incorrect. 4.32 seconds uses only the longer train (180 m) instead of the combined length.
Correct. Relative speed = 150 km/h = 125/3 m/s; combined length 300 m; time = 300/(125/3) = 7.2 s.
items.prompt: Two trains of lengths 120 m and 180 m run towards each other at 60 km/h and 90 km/h respectively. In how many seconds do they completely cross each other?
items.solution: 1. Combined length = 300 m. 2. Relative speed = 60+90 = 150 km/h = 150*5/18 = 125/3 m/s. 3. Time = 300/(125/3) = 900/125 = 7.2 s. Answer D.

explanations: Correct. Effective multiplier = 1.2 (markup) * 0.9 (discount) * 1000/900 (weight cheat) = 1.2, i.e. 20% profit.
Incorrect. 11.11% is the weight cheat alone (1000/900 - 1), ignoring markup and discount.
Incorrect. 8% multiplies markup by discount (1.2*0.9 - 1) but forgets the false weight.
Incorrect. 10% merely reports the discount figure.
items.prompt: A shopkeeper marks his goods 20% above cost price, then gives a 10% discount on the marked price, and also uses a false weight of 900 g instead of 1 kg. What is his overall profit percentage?
items.solution: 1. Take cost Rs. 1000/kg (true). 2. Customer asking 1 kg pays 1000*1.2*0.9 = Rs. 1080 but receives 900 g costing Rs. 900. 3. Profit = 180/900 = 20%. Answer A.

items.prompt: A can finish a job in 12 days and B in 15 days. They work on alternate days, starting with A, one person per day. On which day (counted from the start) is the job completed?
items.solution: 1. A pair of days (A then B) completes 1/12+1/15 = 9/60 = 3/20 of the job. 2. After 12 days (6 pairs): 18/20 = 0.9 done. 3. Day 13 (A): 0.9+1/12 = 59/60 < 1, still short. 4. Day 14 (B) finishes it. Answer: 14

explanations: Incorrect. 73 adds the two counts (24+49) - trailing zeros of a sum come from the smaller exponent, not the sum.
Incorrect. 49 is v5 of 200! alone - the 100! term dominates the sum's factorization.
Correct. v5(100!) = 20+4 = 24 and v5(200!) = 49; factoring 10^24 out leaves a cofactor not divisible by 5, so the sum has exactly 24 zeros.
Incorrect. 20 stops after 100/5, missing the 100/25 = 4 contribution.
items.prompt: How many trailing zeros does 100! + 200! have?
items.solution: 1. Trailing zeros need factors of 10 = 2*5; 5s are scarcer. 2. v5(100!) = 20+4 = 24; v5(200!) = 40+8+1 = 49. 3. 100!+200! = 10^24*(m + 10^25*n) with m not divisible by 5, so exactly 24 factors of 10. Answer C.

explanations: Incorrect. 15 takes the larger mod-9 candidate (a+b = 15, e.g. a = 7, b = 8) without testing divisibility by 8, which it fails.
Correct. Mod 9 forces a+b = 6 or 15; testing last-three-digits mod 8 leaves only (a,b) = (0,6): 056 = 7*8, and digit sum 18. So a+b = 6.
Incorrect. 12 merely adds the fixed digits 3+4+5, ignoring a and b.
Incorrect. It is determined: the mod-8 check collapses the candidates to the single pair (0,6).
items.prompt: A five-digit number 34a5b is divisible by 72. What is a+b?
items.solution: 1. Divisible by 9: 3+4+a+5+b = 12+a+b is a multiple of 9, so a+b = 6 or 15. 2. Divisible by 8: test candidates; (a,b) = (0,6) gives 056 = 7*8 with digit sum 18 - valid. 3. Every a+b = 15 candidate fails mod 8, leaving the unique pair (0,6). 4. a+b = 6. Answer B.

explanations: Incorrect. 126 excludes 0 (C(9,4)) - correct for INCREASING digits, but here 0 can sit last.
Incorrect. 5040 permutes 10 digits taken 4 at a time, counting every order instead of one.
Correct. Choose any 4 distinct digits from 10 (0 allowed, since it lands last and the number stays 4-digit); exactly one arrangement decreases. C(10,4) = 210.
Incorrect. 3024 both excludes 0 and permutes (P(9,4)) - wrong on both counts.
items.prompt: How many 4-digit numbers have strictly decreasing digits from left to right?
items.solution: 1. Pick any 4 distinct digits from 0-9: C(10,4) = 210 sets. 2. Each set has exactly one decreasing arrangement, and 0 (if picked) lands last, so the number stays 4-digit. 3. Hence 210. Answer C.
